test_cases.name: SaaS Launch for Law Firms
test_cases.prompt: We're planning to launch a subscription SaaS product for small law firms at $99/month. Our assumptions are: law firms want cloud-based tools, $99 is affordable, we can acquire customers through LinkedIn ads. What assumptions are we missing?

expectations.text: Output produces a 4-category assumption matrix with sections for (a) Human Only, (b) AI Only, (c) Both, and (d) Emerged During Merge
Output categorizes at least 3 assumptions the user missed (category b items) that are substantive, not trivial
Output assigns risk levels (reasonable, risky, or needs testing) to each assumption
Output identifies at least 2 testable assumptions with concrete test methods, timelines, or decision thresholds
Output distinguishes between contextual assumptions (market, cultural) and structural assumptions (technical, systemic, scale)
Category (d) contains at least 1 genuine emergent assumption that is not a restatement of items from other categories
Output identifies critical path assumptions -- which assumptions, if wrong, would invalidate the entire plan

test_cases.name: PostgreSQL for Real-Time Analytics
test_cases.prompt: Our team decided to use PostgreSQL for our real-time analytics pipeline processing 10M events/day. Help me audit the assumptions behind this choice.

expectations.text: Output produces a 4-category assumption matrix with sections for (a) Human Only, (b) AI Only, (c) Both, and (d) Emerged During Merge
Output categorizes at least 3 assumptions the user missed (category b items) covering structural/technical dimensions
Output assigns risk levels (reasonable, risky, or needs testing) to each assumption
Output identifies at least 2 testable assumptions with concrete test methods such as benchmarks, load tests, or prototypes
Output distinguishes between contextual assumptions (team skills, organizational) and structural assumptions (performance, scalability, data model)
Category (d) contains at least 1 genuine emergent assumption not restated from other categories
Output identifies critical path assumptions -- which assumptions, if wrong, would invalidate the architecture choice

test_cases.name: Career Change - Consulting Business
test_cases.prompt: I'm planning to quit my job and start a consulting business. I think I can replace my income within 6 months. What am I not seeing?

expectations.text: Output produces a 4-category assumption matrix with sections for (a) Human Only, (b) AI Only, (c) Both, and (d) Emerged During Merge
Output categorizes at least 3 assumptions the user missed covering financial, market, and personal dimensions
Output assigns risk levels (reasonable, risky, or needs testing) to each assumption
Output identifies at least 2 testable assumptions with concrete test methods such as freelance trial, client pipeline validation, or financial runway analysis
Output distinguishes between contextual assumptions (personal situation, network) and structural assumptions (market demand, pricing, sales cycle)
Category (d) contains at least 1 genuine emergent assumption not restated from other categories
Output identifies critical path assumptions -- which assumptions, if wrong, would make the career change fail
